Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A normalised, production-standard PostgreSQL schema forms the transactional source of truth for the platform. \\ * Core tables (accounts, instruments, orders, positions) are created with keys, constraints and indexes. \\ * Historical trade structures and representative seed data are in place; each team member can explain the model. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * This is the data foundation every later component builds on. \\ * Snowflake (OLAP) is introduced here as the analytics warehouse Postgres will later feed. \\ * Security focus: parameterised queries (OWASP A03), schema constraints, least-privilege DB roles, no secrets in connection config.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Entities, attributes and relationships for the trading domain are identified. \\ * A clear entity-relationship diagram documents accounts, instruments, orders and positions. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Identify the core entities from the project brief (Account, Instrument, Order, Position) and their relationships. \\  \\ Model cardinality and optionality between entities. \\  \\ Produce an ER diagram and commit it to the repository alongside a short data-dictionary. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Each team member must be able to explain the model at showcase.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The schema is normalised to third normal form with no redundant or transitive dependencies. \\ * Design decisions and any deliberate denormalisation are documented with rationale. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Translate the ER diagram into a normalised relational design (1NF, 2NF, 3NF). \\  \\ Document any justified denormalisation for query performance.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * ACCOUNTS, INSTRUMENTS, ORDERS and POSITIONS tables exist with correct column types. \\ * Primary keys, foreign keys, unique constraints and check constraints enforce integrity. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create the ACCOUNTS table (id BIGINT PK, account_id VARCHAR UNIQUE, holder_name, cash_balance NUMERIC(18,2), status, version, last_updated). \\  \\ Create the ORDERS table (id UUID PK, account_id FK, symbol FK, side, quantity, price, status, idempotency_key UNIQUE, created_on). \\  \\ Create INSTRUMENTS (symbol PK, name, asset_class, currency, tradable) and POSITIONS (account_id FK, symbol FK, quantity, average_cost). \\  \\ Add check constraints (quantity > 0, price > 0, status enumerations) and a unique constraint on idempotency_key. \\  \\ Capture the DDL in a version-controlled script so the database can be recreated. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Use least-privilege roles for the application connection; no superuser credentials in config.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Indexes support the common access patterns (order history by account, positions by account, lookups by symbol). \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add indexes on ORDERS(account_id, created_on) and POSITIONS(account_id, symbol). \\  \\ Verify index usage with EXPLAIN on representative queries.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The schema supports historical trade data alongside the live operational tables. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Design and create structures to retain historical trade records for analytics and audit. \\  \\ Document how historical data is populated and queried.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Representative accounts, instruments, orders and positions are loaded and queryable. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Author a seed-data script inserting realistic accounts, instruments and trades. \\  \\ Confirm referential integrity holds after loading. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Seed data should cover active, suspended and closed accounts and be rich enough to support the Sprint 4 analytics work.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A Python dashboard surfaces at least three business insights over a realistic trading dataset. \\ * Data ingestion is structured as a simple, testable extract-transform-load pipeline. \\ * Data is accessed through APIs and a data-source connection, orienting teams to the operational vs analytical split. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * First orientation to the Fidelity data landscape (operational Postgres vs analytical Snowflake). \\ * Security focus: validation and data-quality checks (OWASP A08), safe handling of sensitive financial data, pytest guards.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A realistic sample trading dataset is added to support analysis. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Source or generate a representative dataset covering trades, accounts and instruments. \\  \\ Document the dataset schema and provenance.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Patterns, anomalies and segments in the dataset are explored and summarised. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Load the dataset with pandas and profile distributions, ranges and null patterns. \\  \\ Produce a one-page EDA summary of findings.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Missing values, incorrect types, malformed dates and outliers are handled explicitly. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement cleaning transforms for missing values, type coercion, date parsing and outlier treatment. \\  \\ Record every cleaning decision so results are reproducible.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * At least three business insights are produced from the dataset. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Compute trade volume (count and value by date). \\  \\ Identify most active accounts and fill rate (filled vs rejected). \\  \\ Compute exposure by instrument and average trade size over a period. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Insights must be explainable to a non-technical stakeholder.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Clear, well-labelled charts communicate the insights to a non-technical audience. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Select appropriate chart types for each insight (matplotlib / seaborn / plotly). \\  \\ Assemble the charts into a simple dashboard view.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Data ingestion is structured as a testable extract-transform-load pipeline. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Structure ingestion into distinct extract, transform and load stages. \\  \\ Load prepared data into the analytical store for reporting. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * ETL is introduced conceptually here, not built to depth; depth comes in Sprint 7 and the DE specialisation.

Summary: Access Fauxnance Data Through a REST API
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Historical price data is pulled from the Fauxnance API, handling auth, pagination and rate limits. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Call GET /candles/{symbol} on the Fauxnance API with the key read from the X-Api-Key environment variable. \\  \\ Handle 429 rate-limit responses gracefully with backoff and load the results for analysis. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Reinforces choosing API access over building a pipeline when appropriate. Keys live in the environment, never in the repository.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * pytest validates the pipeline transforms and outputs and catches bad data early. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write unit tests for the transform functions. \\  \\ Add validation tests that fail on malformed or out-of-range input. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid input transforms to expected output \\ # missing required field is rejected \\ # out-of-range value is flagged \\ # empty dataset handled without error

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A dimensional model for trade analytics is defined in Snowflake. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Define DIM_ACCOUNT, DIM_INSTRUMENT, DIM_DATE and FACT_TRADES. \\  \\ Document the star schema and its grain. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * This schema is the load target for the Sprint 7 batch pipeline. The ANSI schema also runs on DuckDB for teams without a Snowflake account.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The core trading engine is designed with UML and built in clean, SOLID, unit-tested Java. \\ * Domain entities, enums, DTOs and a custom exception hierarchy model the trading domain. \\ * Order placement and settlement logic is standalone and ready to wrap in a service; no DB or API yet. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Pure domain logic; this is the business-logic engine the Sprint 6 service will expose. \\ * Security focus: input validation in the domain model, defensive coding and clean code to minimise the vulnerability surface.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * UML class and sequence diagrams model the trading domain and order lifecycle. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Identify entities, responsibilities and relationships from the requirements. \\  \\ Produce class diagrams (association, aggregation, composition, inheritance). \\  \\ Produce sequence diagrams for order placement and settlement. \\  \\ Peer-review the diagrams and refine.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Account, Instrument, Order and Position entities are implemented in Java. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create Account (id, accountId, holderName, cashBalance, status, version, lastUpdated) with debit(), credit(), isActive(). \\  \\ Create Instrument (id, symbol, name, assetClass, currency, tradable) with isTradable(). \\  \\ Create Order (id, accountId, symbol, side, quantity, price, status, idempotencyKey, createdOn). \\  \\ Create Position (accountId, symbol, quantity, averageCost) with apply() and marketValue().

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * AccountStatus, OrderSide and OrderStatus enums are defined. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create AccountStatus (ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, CLOSED). \\  \\ Create OrderSide (BUY, SELL) and OrderStatus (NEW, FILLED, REJECTED, CANCELLED).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Request and response DTOs carry validation annotations. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create PlaceOrderRequest with @NotNull and @Positive validations. \\  \\ Create OrderResponse, AccountResponse, PositionResponse and ErrorResponse. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid request passes validation \\ # null required field is rejected \\ # non-positive quantity or price is rejected

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A custom exception hierarchy models the domain error conditions. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create AccountNotFoundException and AccountNotActiveException. \\  \\ Create InstrumentNotFoundException. \\  \\ Create InsufficientFundsException and InsufficientHoldingsException. \\  \\ Create DuplicateOrderException for reused idempotency keys.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Buy and sell rules are enforced and positions and cash update atomically. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement order validation (account exists and is ACTIVE, instrument tradable, quantity and price > 0). \\  \\ Implement BUY logic: verify cash balance >= quantity x price, then debit cash and update position. \\  \\ Implement SELL logic: verify held quantity >= order quantity, then credit cash and reduce position. \\  \\ Enforce idempotency using the idempotency key. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # buy succeeds and updates cash and position \\ # buy rejected on insufficient funds \\ # sell rejected on insufficient holdings \\ # order rejected on inactive account \\ # order rejected on unknown or non-tradable instrument \\ # duplicate idempotency key rejected

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Domain logic is covered by meaningful JUnit tests written test-first (red-green-refactor). \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write AccountTest: testDebit_Success, testDebit_InsufficientFunds, testCredit_Success. \\  \\ Write OrderLogicTest: testBuy_Success, testSell_InsufficientHoldings, testReject_InactiveAccount. \\  \\ Write PlaceOrderRequestValidationTest: testValidRequest, testInvalidQuantity, testNullFields. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A single unit test is one class, one method, one execution path; cover error paths as isolated tests.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Sprint 5 logic is wrapped in a layered Spring Boot service with MyBatis persistence to Postgres. \\ * REST endpoints implement contracts/trade-api.yaml and the service is Dockerised. \\ * Protected routes validate JWTs issued by the provided Node auth stub; the real auth service replaces it in Sprint 8. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * First service exposing the core logic via an API. \\ * In Sprint 6 there is no Trade Executor, so POST /api/v1/orders fills synchronously and returns FILLED or REJECTED. Sprint 7 changes it to return NEW. \\ * Security focus: Spring Security JWT validation on protected endpoints, Bean Validation on DTOs, safe error handling with no stack-trace leakage (OWASP A01, A05).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A Spring Boot project is bootstrapped with the required dependencies and configuration. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create the Spring Boot project and add web, validation, MyBatis and OpenAPI dependencies. \\  \\ Configure application properties (datasource, server port, logging).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service implements the order and account endpoints defined in contracts/trade-api.yaml, contract-first. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Work to the OpenAPI spec for POST /api/v1/orders, DELETE /api/v1/orders/{id} and the account endpoints. \\  \\ Match the request/response schemas and the error envelope in the spec exactly. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Contract-first: the spec drives the implementation and is the binding reference every consumer generates its client from later.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service follows a clean controller to service to repository layering. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Establish controller, service and repository layers with clear responsibilities. \\  \\ Wire dependency injection between the layers, keeping SQL out of controllers and HTTP types out of the domain.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * MyBatis mappers persist and query against the Sprint 3 Postgres schema using parameterised queries. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement MyBatis mappers for accounts, orders and positions. \\  \\ Use parameterised statements throughout to prevent injection. \\  \\ Map result sets to the domain and DTO objects. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # order row inserted and retrievable \\ # account and positions read correctly \\ # mapper throws on constraint violation

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * OrderService wraps the core logic with transactional order processing. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement placeOrder(PlaceOrderRequest), cancelOrder(orderId), validateOrder() and executeOrder(). \\  \\ Annotate order placement with @Transactional so cash and position update atomically. \\  \\ Apply optimistic locking using the account version. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # place order commits cash and position together \\ # failed order rolls back with no partial write \\ # concurrent update detected via optimistic lock

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * AccountService exposes account, balance, positions and order-history reads. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement getAccount(id), getBalance(id), getPositions(id) and getOrders(id). \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # account details returned for valid id \\ # not-found error for unknown account

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * POST /api/v1/orders places an order and DELETE /api/v1/orders/{id} cancels a working order. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement POST /api/v1/orders returning orderId, status and echo of the order. \\  \\ Implement DELETE /api/v1/orders/{id} returning the updated order status. \\  \\ Return conflict (ORD-409) when cancelling a filled or already-cancelled order. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # request mapping invalid (400) \\ # server error (500) \\ # order placed and filled successfully \\ # order rejected on business-rule failure \\ # working order cancelled successfully \\ # cancel of filled order returns conflict \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Test the flow to place and cancel orders using the real controller, service and MyBatis persistence against Postgres.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * GET endpoints expose account details, cash balance, positions and order history. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement GET /api/v1/accounts/{id}, /balance, /positions and /orders. \\  \\ Shape responses via the account and position DTOs. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # request mapping invalid (400) \\ # server error (500) \\ # account, balance, positions and orders returned successfully \\ # unknown account returns not found \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Test the read flows using the real controller, service and persistence classes.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Incoming requests are validated with Bean Validation and responses are shaped by DTOs. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Apply @Valid and Bean Validation constraints on request DTOs. \\  \\ Return VAL-422 for invalid input. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid request accepted \\ # invalid quantity or price returns 422 \\ # null required field returns 422

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A @ControllerAdvice maps domain exceptions to the documented error catalogue with no stack-trace leakage. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement @ControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler methods. \\  \\ Map exceptions to ACC-404, ACC-403, INS-404, ORD-400, ORD-409, VAL-422 and AUTH-401 with correct HTTP status. \\  \\ Return the ErrorResponse shape and log the error internally without exposing internals. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # account not found maps to ACC-404 (404) \\ # inactive account maps to ACC-403 (403) \\ # insufficient funds maps to ORD-400 (400) \\ # duplicate order maps to ORD-409 (409) \\ # invalid input maps to VAL-422 (422)

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service emits structured logs suitable for auditing order activity. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add structured logging around order placement, cancellation and errors. \\  \\ Ensure no secrets or sensitive payloads are logged.

Summary: JWT Validation Against the Provided Auth Stub
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Protected /api/v1/** routes validate a JWT issued by the provided Node auth stub and reject missing or invalid tokens with AUTH-401. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add a Spring Security filter that verifies the HS256 signature, expiry and claims of tokens from the provided Node auth stub, using the shared development secret from JWT_SECRET. \\  \\ Reject a token whose accountId claim does not match the account being addressed with ACC-403. \\  \\ Return AUTH-401 for missing, malformed, expired or wrongly signed tokens. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The auth stub is provided in the starter material, not built. It is a fixture with no tests to write. \\ * The stub is used through Sprint 7 and replaced by the real auth service in Sprint 8; the swap is configuration only.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service runs as a Docker image built with a multi-stage Dockerfile. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write a multi-stage Dockerfile that builds and packages the service. \\  \\ Verify the containerised service starts and serves requests.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Three Kafka topics (orders, trade-events, market-data) move trade events between services as the real-time backbone, keyed and partitioned per contracts/kafka-topics.md. \\ * The Trade REST API publishes accepted orders to orders and returns NEW; teams build the Trade Executor that consumes orders, prices each against a live Fauxnance quote, applies the fill rules and publishes the outcome to trade-events. \\ * A market-data poller publishes Fauxnance quotes onto market-data, and a batch ETL pipeline loads the analytics warehouse with data-quality checks. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * There is no provided Broker Simulator. The whole execution path, the Trade Executor, the fill logic and the market-data poller, is the participants' to build. \\ * Real-time plus batch data backbone. \\ * Security focus: DevSecOps in CI (SAST, dependency scanning, secret detection) and SonarQube quality gates (OWASP A06, A08).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The orders, trade-events and market-data topics are created with the documented keys, partition counts and retention. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create orders (key accountId as a string, 3 partitions, 7-day retention) and trade-events (key accountId, 3 partitions, 30-day retention). \\  \\ Create market-data (key symbol, 6 partitions, 1-day retention). \\  \\ Create topics explicitly at startup rather than relying on auto-creation, and record the partition and key choices. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Key orders and trade-events by accountId so all events for one account stay ordered on one partition. Key market-data by symbol. Never key by order identifier.

Summary: Order Publishing from the Trade REST API
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * From Sprint 7, POST /api/v1/orders persists the order as NEW, publishes an ORDER_PLACED event to orders and returns NEW. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add a producer with acks=all and enable.idempotence=true that publishes the standard envelope and the ORDER_PLACED payload after the database commit. \\  \\ Change the endpoint to record the order as NEW and stop filling synchronously; both behaviours remain valid under contracts/trade-api.yaml. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # order persisted then event published after commit \\ # publish failure leaves a recoverable committed order \\ # rolled-back order publishes no event \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Publish after the commit, never inside the transaction. A published event for a rolled-back order is unrecoverable; a committed order not yet published is recoverable by replaying the order table.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A standalone Trade Executor consumes orders in consumer group trade-executor with manual offset commits. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build the executor as a separate deployable Kafka consumer subscribed to orders. \\  \\ Disable auto-commit; process the message, then commit the offset. \\  \\ Set an explicit group.id of trade-executor and handle partition rebalancing. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # message consumed and offset committed after processing \\ # rebalance reassigns partitions without losing a message \\ # consumer count above the partition count leaves an idle consumer \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * There is no Broker Simulator. The executor is the execution engine and it is built here, not called.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The executor prices each order against a live Fauxnance quote, applies the marketability gate, re-checks funds and holdings at execution time, and updates order, cash and position in one transaction. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Fetch a delayed quote with GET /quotes/{symbol}, reading the key from the X-Api-Key environment variable. \\  \\ Apply the marketability gate: fill in full when a BUY limit price is at or above the quote, or a SELL limit price is at or below it; otherwise reject. \\  \\ Re-check at execution time that the account is ACTIVE, cash covers a BUY and holdings cover a SELL, since state may have changed since acceptance. \\  \\ Update orders, cash and position atomically and publish ORDER_FILLED or ORDER_REJECTED with executedPrice, cashDelta, positionQuantityAfter and averageCostAfter to trade-events. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # marketable buy fills at the quoted price and debits cash once \\ # non-marketable order rejected with reason PRICE_NOT_MET \\ # buy rejected with reason INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS when cash no longer covers it \\ # sell rejected when holdings no longer cover it \\ # a rejection is published to trade-events, not swallowed \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Partial fills are out of scope; OrderStatus has no state for them, so fill in full or reject. Fill rules are the team's design decision within the contract business rules.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Replaying a consumed ORDER_PLACED message does not double-debit an account, and poison messages are routed to a dead-letter topic without blocking the partition. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Guard the state transition with UPDATE orders SET ... WHERE id = ? AND status = 'NEW' and treat zero rows affected as already handled. \\  \\ Route a message that fails deserialisation or validation to orders.DLT on the first attempt, with the original message as the value and the failure reason in a header. \\  \\ Retry a transient failure (for example Fauxnance returning 503) with backoff and dead-letter it only once the retry budget is spent. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # duplicate delivery leaves cash and position unchanged \\ # malformed message dead-lettered on first attempt \\ # transient failure retried with backoff then succeeds \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The platform runs at-least-once. Duplicates happen; the guarded transition makes reprocessing safe. Demonstrating a replay that does not move the balance twice is the Sprint 7 acceptance check.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A poller calls Fauxnance batch quotes on an interval and publishes one QUOTE message per symbol onto market-data, staying inside the daily quota. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Poll only held and watched symbols, batching up to 25 per call with GET /quotes?symbols=A,B,C, which counts as one request against the 2000-per-day quota. \\  \\ Publish one message per symbol keyed by symbol, not one message per batch, so per-symbol ordering holds. \\  \\ Cache last prices and back off when GET /usage shows the quota is close to exhausted. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # a batch of 25 symbols is one Fauxnance request \\ # one Kafka message published per symbol \\ # polling limited to held and watched symbols \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Fauxnance has no stream. This poller is what creates the market-data stream that Sprint 10 extensions consume. The UI never calls Fauxnance, because that would ship a key to the browser.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Trade data is extracted from Postgres, transformed and loaded into the analytics warehouse defined in Sprint 4. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement extract, transform and load stages for trade data. \\  \\ Load the FACT_TRADES and dimension tables. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # full load populates the warehouse \\ # transform handles nulls and type mismatches \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Teams without a Snowflake account load the same ANSI schema into DuckDB.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The pipeline handles errors with retries and idempotency so reruns are safe. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add retry logic with backoff on transient failures. \\  \\ Make loads idempotent (incremental vs full) so reprocessing does not duplicate data. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # transient failure retried then succeeds \\ # rerun does not duplicate loaded rows

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Records are validated and schema-checked; bad records are routed to a dead-letter store without killing the pipeline. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add validation and schema checks on inbound records. \\  \\ Route invalid records to a dead-letter store and alert. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid record loaded \\ # invalid record routed to dead-letter \\ # pipeline continues after a bad record

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Characterisation tests capture existing behaviour of the planted starter codebase as a safety net before refactoring. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write characterisation tests around the provided starter codebase. \\  \\ Apply the first set of refactors (extract method, replace conditional, introduce parameter object) with tests proving behaviour is unchanged. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The us-ireland starter code carries intentional defects and legacy patterns. Write the characterisation tests before changing any of it.

Summary: SonarQube Quality Gates & DevSecOps in CI
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * SonarQube analysis and DevSecOps checks run in GitHub Actions and enforce quality and security gates. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Wire SonarQube analysis into the pipeline and interpret findings. \\  \\ Add SAST, dependency scanning and secret detection to CI. \\  \\ Configure quality gates that fail the build on threshold breaches.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Sprint 4 Python analytics dashboard is updated to consume from both the real-time stream and the batch warehouse. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Extend the Sprint 4 dashboard to read real-time and batch sources. \\  \\ Reconcile the two views for consistency.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A centralised NestJS auth service issues and validates JWTs with credentials hashed in Postgres, implementing contracts/auth-api.yaml. \\ * At least one Spring Boot route is protected by real tokens end-to-end, with live OpenAPI docs. \\ * The auth flow is reviewed against the auth-focused OWASP items. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The security keystone of the platform. It replaces the provided Node auth stub used in Sprints 6 and 7. \\ * Security focus: password hashing, JWT issuance and validation, defence against token leakage, replay and timing attacks (OWASP A07, A01).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A modular, layered NestJS service is scaffolded in TypeScript with controller, service and repository layers. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Scaffold the NestJS project with modules, controllers and providers. \\  \\ Establish the layered structure and dependency injection.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The auth endpoints implement contracts/auth-api.yaml, contract-first. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Work to the login, register, refresh and current-user contracts in the OpenAPI spec. \\  \\ Match the token and error response schemas exactly.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The auth service exposes register, login and refresh REST endpoints. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement register(), login() and refresh() in AuthService. \\  \\ Validate inputs with class-validator and class-transformer. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # request mapping invalid (400) \\ # server error (500) \\ # registration succeeds for new user \\ # registration rejected for existing user \\ # login succeeds and returns a token \\ # login fails on bad credentials \\ # refresh issues a new token for a valid refresh token \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Test register, login and refresh against the real service and Postgres persistence.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Passwords are hashed with argon2id or bcrypt at cost 12 or above using per-user salts; plaintext is never stored. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Hash credentials with argon2id or bcrypt and store only the hash and salt. \\  \\ Verify passwords using a constant-time comparison. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # correct password verifies \\ # incorrect password fails verification \\ # weak hashing (MD5/SHA) is not used

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A signed JWT is issued on successful login carrying exactly the claims contract: sub, accountId, roles, iat, exp, iss. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement TokenService.issue() building a signed HS256 token (header, payload, signature). \\  \\ Set the 15-minute access-token expiry and required claims; sign with the shared secret from JWT_SECRET. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # token issued with correct claims and expiry \\ # token signature verifies with the service key

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Tokens are validated on protected routes and rejected when invalid or expired. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement TokenService.verify() and decode(). \\  \\ Reject expired, tampered or malformed tokens with AUTH-401. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid token accepted \\ # expired token rejected \\ # tampered signature rejected \\ # malformed token rejected

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Guards protect routes and a decorator extracts the authenticated user from the token. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement an auth guard on protected endpoints. \\  \\ Add a decorator that extracts the user from the validated token. \\  \\ Add interceptors as needed for the request lifecycle. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # guard blocks unauthenticated request \\ # guard allows authenticated request \\ # user correctly extracted from token

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Refresh tokens rotate on every use and the presented token stops working immediately; reuse revokes the chain. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Store refresh tokens server-side and issue a new one on every refresh, invalidating the presented token. \\  \\ Treat a refresh token presented twice as theft: revoke every refresh token for that user and return AUTH-401. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # refresh issues a new pair and the old refresh token stops working \\ # a consumed refresh token presented again is rejected \\ # reuse revokes the whole chain

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service uses structured logging (winston or pino) without logging sensitive data. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Add structured logging around auth events. \\  \\ Ensure credentials and tokens are never written to logs, including inside error objects.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The auth flow is reviewed against auth-specific OWASP items and hardened. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Review for broken authentication and broken access control (OWASP A07, A01). \\  \\ Confirm an unknown user and a wrong password return the same body, status and comparable timing. \\  \\ Assess and mitigate token leakage, replay and timing attacks and weak secrets, and document findings and remediations.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Meaningful Jest tests cover the service, guards and token handling. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write unit tests mocking providers and testing guards. \\  \\ Cover token issuance, validation and error paths. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # guard unit test blocks and allows correctly \\ # token issuance produces valid token \\ # validation rejects expired and tampered tokens

Summary: Integration: Protect a Spring Boot Route End-to-End
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The provided auth stub is replaced so at least one Spring Boot route is protected by the real auth service end-to-end. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Replace the Node auth stub with real token validation against the auth service, a configuration change only. \\  \\ Publish live OpenAPI docs served by the running auth service. \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Test the end-to-end flow: obtain a token from the auth service, call a protected Spring Boot route, and confirm rejection without a valid token.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Angular frontend delivers an authenticated login flow end-to-end and the core trading views. \\ * The UI consumes the Trade and Auth REST APIs via typed clients generated from the contracts. \\ * Core journeys are covered by unit and Playwright end-to-end tests. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * User-facing app; with this the full stack is complete. \\ * Security focus: JWT interceptors attach bearer tokens, route guards protect authenticated routes, output encoding prevents XSS (OWASP A03, A01).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Angular app is scaffolded with standalone components, routing and signals. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create the Angular project with standalone components and routing. \\  \\ Set up the build tooling and dev server.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Users can log in, the token is stored, and a JWT interceptor attaches it to outgoing requests. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement AuthService with login(), logout(), isAuthenticated() and getToken(). \\  \\ Add a JWT interceptor that attaches the bearer token to API calls and not to Fauxnance or third-party calls. \\  \\ Store the token securely and clear it on logout. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # login stores token and authenticates \\ # interceptor attaches token to requests \\ # logout clears the session \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Verify the login flow against the real auth service end-to-end.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Route guards protect authenticated routes and redirect unauthenticated users to login. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement a route guard on protected routes. \\  \\ Redirect unauthenticated access to the login screen. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # guard blocks unauthenticated navigation \\ # guard allows authenticated navigation

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Typed API clients are generated from the Sprint 6 and Sprint 8 OpenAPI contracts and consumed by the app. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Generate typed clients from the Trade and Auth OpenAPI contracts, not by hand. \\  \\ Build a service layer that consumes the generated clients.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The login screen submits credentials to the auth service and shows an error alert on failure. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build LoginComponent with username and password inputs and a login button. \\  \\ Show an error alert on authentication failure and redirect on success. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid credentials log in and redirect \\ # invalid credentials show error alert \\ # empty fields blocked by validation

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The dashboard shows a welcome banner, cash balance, positions summary and navigation actions. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build DashboardComponent with a balance card and positions summary from the account API. \\  \\ Add navigation buttons to the order ticket and blotter, plus logout. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # balance and positions render from the API \\ # navigation buttons route correctly

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The order ticket places an order via the Trade API with client-side validation and a result message. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build OrderTicketComponent with instrument, side (BUY/SELL), quantity (> 0) and price inputs. \\  \\ Submit to the order endpoint and show a success or error message, rendering every error code from the catalogue. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid order submits and shows success \\ # invalid quantity blocked by validation \\ # business-rule rejection shows error message \\ # an order still NEW is handled \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Add a Playwright test covering the place-order journey end-to-end.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The blotter lists orders with formatted dates, coloured side, values and status badges. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build BlotterComponent rendering the order table from the order-history API. \\  \\ Format dates, colour BUY green and SELL red, and show status badges (New, Filled, Rejected, Cancelled). \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # order history renders as expected \\ # an order sitting at NEW is shown \\ # empty history handled gracefully

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Unit tests and Playwright end-to-end tests cover the core user journeys. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write unit tests for components, services and pipes. \\  \\ Write Playwright tests for login, place order and view history. \\  \\ Confirm no API key and no secret is present in the built bundle. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Judge coverage on risk and meaning, not as a percentage.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The team selects exactly one extension microservice from the catalogue of six and integrates it end-to-end with the platform. \\ * A dedicated security-review checkpoint applies OWASP principles to the new service. \\ * A quality pass and an architecture decision log prepare the extension for the showcase. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Distinctive, team-selected capability built on the shipped trading core. US and Ireland policy is exactly one mandatory extension; assessment is on depth, integration quality and the security review for that one service. \\ * The extension stories below are the catalogue. The team builds one of them.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The team selects exactly one extension from the catalogue and confirms its scope and integration plan on day one. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Choose one extension from the six: Portfolio and P&L; Trade Advice and Signals; Watchlists and Price Alerts; Customer Notifications; Customer Preferences and Personalisation; Automated Strategy Execution. \\  \\ Confirm how the chosen service authenticates with the platform JWT and integrates with Kafka or the Trade REST API and the UI. \\  \\ Agree the backlog, task allocation and integration checkpoints for the week. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Dependency warning: Customer Notifications needs Customer Preferences (a notification needs a channel to route to), and Watchlists alerting needs Customer Notifications (a triggered threshold must be delivered somewhere). A team choosing either of those builds the pair, not one half.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A Portfolio and P&L service exposes consolidated holdings, cost basis and realised/unrealised P&L via REST, implementing contracts/portfolio-api.yaml. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build the service consuming trade-events (group portfolio-service) and market-data, and pricing from Fauxnance quotes. \\  \\ Compute holdings, cost basis and realised/unrealised P&L across accounts. \\  \\ Expose the results via a REST API and integrate end-to-end. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # P&L computed correctly for a known trade set \\ # realised vs unrealised split correct \\ # unauthorised access rejected \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Catalogue option. Builds on trade-events (S7) and market-data (S7); independent of the other extensions.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A Trade Advice service surfaces research-driven BUY/SELL/HOLD signals with the reasoning behind each. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build the service consuming trade-events and market-data (group advice-service) and Fauxnance candles. \\  \\ Generate BUY/SELL/HOLD signals against holdings and watchlist with explanations. \\  \\ Integrate with the UI or API end-to-end. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # signal generated with reasoning \\ # no signal when data insufficient \\ # unauthorised access rejected \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Catalogue option. Builds on market and price data; analytics layer.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * An automation service runs rules-based strategies against the market-data stream and acts when conditions are met. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build the service consuming market-data (group strategy-service). \\  \\ Implement moving-average crossover and Bollinger-band triggers. \\  \\ Place resulting orders via the Trade REST API (S6). \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # strategy triggers on a crossover condition \\ # no action when conditions not met \\ # order placed through the Trade API on trigger \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Catalogue option. Builds on the market-data stream (S7) and Trade REST API (S6). In production this would sit behind suitability and risk controls.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A notifications service delivers proactive real-time alerts via the customer's preferred channel. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build the service consuming trade-events (group notification-service) and Customer Preferences. \\  \\ Deliver trade confirmations, price moves, statements and corporate-action alerts. \\  \\ Route to the preferred channel (email, SMS or in-app). \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # alert delivered on a qualifying event \\ # channel selection honoured \\ # no alert when preference disables it \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Catalogue option. Depends on Customer Preferences: a notification cannot be routed without a channel. Choose the pair, not just this.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A watchlist service lets customers track instruments and trigger real-time threshold alerts. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build the service consuming the market-data stream (group watchlist-service). \\  \\ Support watchlists and price or volatility thresholds. \\  \\ Trigger alerts via the Notifications service, not to a log. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # threshold breach triggers an alert \\ # no alert below threshold \\ # watchlist scoped to the authenticated user \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Catalogue option. Alerting depends on Customer Notifications, which depends on Customer Preferences. A team choosing this builds all three.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A preferences service persists customer settings and applies them at next login. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build the service consuming the Auth and profile service (S8) with persistence. \\  \\ Persist default accounts, selections and alert channels. \\  \\ Apply preferences at next login. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # preferences saved and retrieved \\ # preferences applied on login \\ # preferences scoped to the authenticated user \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Catalogue option. Customer Notifications and Watchlists both depend on this, so a team building those starts here.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A dedicated security review applies OWASP principles to the new service. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Review authorisation, input validation and secure inter-service calls, and confirm the service verifies the JWT itself rather than trusting an upstream check. \\  \\ Remediate findings before the showcase.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The extension passes SonarQube quality gates with meaningful test coverage and refactoring applied. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Run SonarQube and address quality-gate findings. \\  \\ Review test coverage and refactor as needed.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Key technical decisions are captured to tell the extension's story at the showcase. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Log the architecture decisions and the rationale behind them. \\  \\ Prepare the showcase narrative for the extension.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Angular build is deployed to AWS (S3 plus CloudFront) with origin access control. \\ * The build to upload to invalidate deployment cycle is automated. \\ * Authenticated flows are validated in the live environment and demonstrated at the final showcase. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A live, deployed cloud home. AWS scope is IAM, the AWS CLI, S3 and CloudFront only. \\ * A Fidelity platform SME briefs teams on Fidelity-specific AWS guardrails before hands-on work; that is a briefing, not a lab. \\ * Security focus: private S3 reachable only via CloudFront, IAM least privilege, TLS enforced, no long-lived credentials committed (OWASP A05).

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * An AWS account, IAM basics and region are configured for the deployment. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Set up the account, IAM users/roles and select a region. \\  \\ Apply least-privilege IAM policies scoped to the bucket and distribution, with no long-lived keys in the repository.
*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The AWS CLI is authenticated and access is verified. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Configure and authenticate the AWS CLI. \\  \\ Run first commands to verify access.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The Angular production build is deployed to a private S3 bucket. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Produce the Angular production build. \\  \\ Upload the build artefacts to the S3 bucket.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The S3 bucket is private and reachable only through CloudFront via origin access control. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Configure origin access control so the bucket is not publicly readable. \\  \\ Confirm direct S3 access is denied while CloudFront access works.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A CloudFront distribution fronts the bucket and serves the app over HTTPS. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Stand up a CloudFront distribution with the S3 origin. \\  \\ Configure behaviours and cache policies and enforce TLS/HTTPS.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Authenticated flows are verified end-to-end in the live environment. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Load the deployed app via CloudFront and complete the login and place-order journeys. \\  \\ Confirm tokens and protected routes behave correctly in production. \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Run an end-to-end check of the authenticated journey against the live deployment.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The build to upload to invalidate cycle is scripted and repeatable. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write a deployment script (bash or a GitHub Actions workflow) that builds, uploads and invalidates the cache. \\  \\ Verify a clean run from a fresh checkout.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The team demonstrates the live, working system to Fidelity leaders, instructors and peers. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Prepare and rehearse the showcase: the platform, the chosen extension, design decisions, Copilot usage and code quality. \\  \\ Present the live system and handle Q&A with the panel.

Summary: DE Specialisation Week 1: ETL Pipeline Engineering & Orchestration
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Sprint 3, 4 and 7 data work is taken to deep pipeline engineering: ETL, data quality and orchestration. \\ * Participants build incremental, idempotent load pipelines with SCD handling and data-quality gates. \\ * An end-to-end pipeline moves Postgres trade data to a validated, transformed Snowflake table, orchestrated by Airflow. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Optional two-week extension on the unified core.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * An incremental load pipeline moves trades from Postgres to Snowflake with upsert and SCD handling. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement incremental patterns (append, upsert via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT). \\  \\ Implement SCD Type 1 (overwrite) and Type 2 (history) where each applies to financial data. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # new records appended \\ # changed record upserted \\ # SCD Type 2 preserves history

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The pipeline correctly handles late-arriving and out-of-order records. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Detect and reconcile late-arriving data. \\  \\ Order records deterministically before load. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # late record merged correctly \\ # out-of-order records reconciled

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Validation-as-code with dead-letter queues and appropriate alerting protects the pipeline. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement validation with Great Expectations or Pandera. \\  \\ Route bad records to a dead-letter queue and alert (fail hard or warn appropriately). \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid record passes checks \\ # invalid record routed to dead-letter \\ # alert raised on failure threshold

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * An Airflow DAG orchestrates the incremental Postgres to Snowflake pipeline with scheduling and retries. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build a DAG with tasks, operators, scheduling, dependencies and trigger rules. \\  \\ Configure retries, SLAs and failure alerts; extend with a data-quality task and a dead-letter branch. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # DAG runs on schedule \\ # failed task retries per policy \\ # quality failure branches to dead-letter

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The team assesses the Sprint 3 schema for CDC readiness and understands low-latency capture. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Review WAL and logical replication concepts. \\  \\ Inspect the Sprint 3 Postgres schema for CDC readiness.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * pytest covers pipeline transforms as units and source-to-target as integration. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write unit tests for transformation functions. \\  \\ Write integration tests validating source to target. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # transform unit test passes \\ # source-to-target integration verified \\ # deliberate data-quality failure is caught

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The team is introduced to transformation-as-code with dbt (models, tests, lineage). \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Introduce dbt models, tests and lineage in the analytical layer.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * An end-to-end ETL pipeline moves Postgres trade data to a validated, transformed Snowflake analytics table, orchestrated by Airflow with data-quality gates and automated retry. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Assemble extract, transform, validate and load into a single orchestrated pipeline. \\  \\ Add data-quality gates and automated retry on failure. \\  \\ Document data lineage and a runbook. \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Run the full pipeline end-to-end and demonstrate a caught data-quality failure and a successful retry.

Summary: DE Specialisation Week 2: Real-Time Integration, Kafka & the Analytical Estate
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Sprint 7 Kafka foundations extend into real-time integration, schema governance and a served analytical estate. \\ * Participants operate advanced Kafka, govern events with Schema Registry and Avro, and build stateful stream processing. \\ * Real-time and batch views feed the same analytical layer, served in PowerBI. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Optional two-week extension on the unified core.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Consumer groups, partition assignment, rebalancing and delivery semantics are applied correctly. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Configure consumer groups and observe partition assignment and rebalancing. \\  \\ Apply at-most-once, at-least-once and exactly-once semantics where each fits financial data. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # rebalance handled without message loss \\ # exactly-once path verified \\ # consumer lag observed under load

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Typed events use Avro with schemas registered and evolved safely. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Define and register Avro schemas for trade events. \\  \\ Evolve a schema (add a field) with backward/forward/full compatibility and no consumer breakage. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # Avro event produced and consumed \\ # compatible schema change does not break consumers \\ # incompatible change is rejected

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Stateless and stateful stream processing with windowing produces real-time trade aggregations. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement stateless transforms (filter, map, branch). \\  \\ Implement stateful aggregations with tumbling, hopping and session windows. \\  \\ Build a real-time trade aggregation (count and value per instrument per minute) and windowed volume alerting. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # windowed aggregation correct \\ # late event handled by the window policy \\ # alert fires on a volume threshold

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A Kafka Connect JDBC source connector streams from the Sprint 3 Postgres schema. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Configure a JDBC source connector on the Postgres schema. \\  \\ Verify records flow into the target topic.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Real-time and batch are connected via the Lambda/Kappa patterns and sinked to Snowflake. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Sink Kafka trade events to Snowflake via the Week 1 pipeline. \\  \\ Feed the same analytical layer from both real-time and batch sources.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Reconciliation ensures the batch and streaming views of the same data agree. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement reconciliation between operational (Postgres) and analytical (Snowflake) stores. \\  \\ Surface and explain any discrepancies. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # batch and streaming totals agree \\ # injected discrepancy detected

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Kafka traffic is secured with TLS and SASL authentication. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Enable TLS in transit and SASL authentication. \\  \\ Verify unauthenticated clients are rejected.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A PowerBI dashboard serves a star-schema trade model from Snowflake with DAX measures. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Connect PowerBI to Snowflake (DirectQuery vs Import) and build a star-schema model. \\  \\ Author DAX measures with time-intelligence (YTD, MTD, rolling averages). \\  \\ Build a trade analytics dashboard on the Snowflake layer.

*Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Trade events flow to Kafka, are stream-processed, sinked to Snowflake and surfaced in PowerBI, with batch and real-time feeding the same analytical layer. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Assemble the real-time path: produce to Kafka, stream-process, sink to Snowflake, surface in PowerBI. \\  \\ Confirm the Week 1 batch pipeline and the real-time stream feed the same analytical layer. \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Demonstrate the end-to-end real-time and batch integration with a design walkthrough and code review.
